newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb rocks French premier Juppe's mayoral offices.
newsitem.headline: Bomb rocks French premier Juppe's mayoral offices.

text.p: A bomb damaged the mayoral offices of French Prime Minister Alain Juppe in Bordeaux overnight, the city's prosecutor said on Sunday.

Patrice Davost told reporters that a powerful device exploded at 11.41 p.m. (2141 GMT) at the elegant city hall. It caused no casualties and the centre-right Juppe was not in the southwestern port city at the time.
There was no immediate indication of who might have set off the device.
Davost said no threats had been received before the bomb shattered windows in the ornate reception hall of the building. No one had claimed responsibility.
The prosecutor gave no details on the make-up of the bomb.
Police said the explosion had probably been caused by a bomb placed at ground level beneath the windows of the building.
The blast blew out French windows leading into the reception hall, damaged furniture inside the building and shattered the windows of the city hall and nearby buildings.

Juppe, who took office as prime minister early last year, regularly visits Bordeaux but he does not reside at the city hall. He had left Bordeaux on Saturday afternoon to return to Paris and was expected to return to Bordeaux on Sunday morning, Juppe's local deputy Didier Cazadone said.
"This is distasteful. Explosives have never been a method of expression," Cazadone said.
"The office of the mayor is slightly hit. The reception hall is symbolic and that's where Alain Juppe was meeting people (on Saturday) morning," he added.
Police sealed off the area and searched through the upper floors of the building.
A wave of bombings, chiefly in Paris, hit France last year. The attacks were blamed on Moslem fundamentalists angered by France's support for Algerian authorities.

Separatist guerrillas have in recent weeks set off bombs in the French Mediterranean island of Corsica in a long campaign for more autonomy from the mainland. They recently threatened to carry out attacks on the mainland.
